### Career Regular-Season Points Per Game

* **Michael Jordan:** 30.1 points per game across 1,072 regular-season games [jordan_playoffs_560], [T1].
* **LeBron James:** 26.8 points per game across 1,622 regular-season games [lebron_playoffs_3440], [T1].

---

### Tradeoffs and Context

* **Scoring Rate vs. Longevity/Volume:** Michael Jordan holds the higher per-game scoring average, averaging 3.3 more points per contest [T1]. In contrast, LeBron James has maintained a high scoring average (26.8 PPG) over a considerably larger regular-season sample size (1,622 games compared to Jordan's 1,072 games) [lebron_playoffs_3440], [jordan_playoffs_560].
* **Scoring Milestones:** Jordan reached higher scoring thresholds in a larger percentage of his games—for example, scoring 30+ points in 52.4% of regular-season games and 40+ points in 16.1% [jordan_playoffs_560], compared to LeBron scoring 30+ points in 35.6% and 40+ points in 4.9% of regular-season games [lebron_playoffs_3440].

---

### Factual Evidence vs. Subjective GOAT Judgments

* **Factual Evidence:** Jordan averaged more points per game in the regular season (30.1 to 26.8) [T1], while James has played over 500 more regular-season games while maintaining a 26.8 PPG pace [lebron_playoffs_3440], [jordan_playoffs_560].
* **Subjective Assessment:** Determining which player holds the advantage overall depends on subjective valuation—prioritizing Jordan's higher per-game scoring rate and peak frequencies versus prioritizing James's sustained scoring efficiency across extended career longevity.
